newsitem.title: USA: Triton has 4th Gulf of Thailand natgas find.
newsitem.headline: Triton has 4th Gulf of Thailand natgas find.

text.p: Triton Energy Ltd said Tuesday it had discovered a fourth major natural-gas field, the Bumi, on Block A-18 in the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Development Area in the Gulf of Thailand.
The Bumi-1 discovery well exhibited 403 feet of net natural gas pay, one of the best wells drilled on Block A-18, based on the results of electronic logs, Triton said.

"Preliminary indications are that the Bumi Field could be one of the largest fields discovered to date on Block A-18. Bumi-1 has shown some of the most prolific and thickest reservoirs seen on the block," Triton's statement said.
Stating only four of six planned flow tests of the Bumi-1 have been completed, it said tests continue in even more prolific shallow reservoir sands.

Results from the initial tests cover 151 feet of the well's net pay, or 37 percent the total feet in the well. Those show a combined daily flow rate of 51 million cubic feet of natural gas and 295 barrels of condensate.

The four selected intervals were between 4,130 and 7,676 feet. The tests were conducted through choke sizes ranging from 1/2-inch to two inches at flowing tubing pressures between 188 and 1,955 pounds per square inch.
The condensate ranged from 38 to 51 degrees gravity and the natural gas tested from the for zones has one of the lowest carbon dioxide contents of all wells on the block.

"When testing is completed, we anticipate that this well could have the highest total gas flow test of any well drilled to date on the block," Triton said. "This well has exhibited more net pay in these shallow sands than previously seen in any other well on Block A-18."
The Bumi-1 is located about 14 kilometers (9 miles) east of the Cakerawala Field and adjacent to the Suriya Field. The Bumi-1 was drilled in some 184 feet of water to a total depth of 9,279 feet.
This is the fourth discovery well and the ninth successful well drilled on Block A-18 by the operator, Carigali-Triton Operating Co which is jointly owned by Triton and Petronas.
